   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 16, 2020

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Ding
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT MANAGER DOMENICA
  MEGERDICHIAN

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 27, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 2, 2020.
  3. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 2, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 16, 2020  2
   Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2020

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of May 2020.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for May 2020.

  D. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2020-2021

  The City of San Gabriel conducts its investment activities in compliance with
  the Statement of Investment Policy which is required to be reviewed and
  adopted annually by the City Council. This policy provides guidelines for
  prudent investing, emphasizing safety, liquidity and yield, in that order. The
  Policy is formulated using the provisions of California Government Code
  Section 53601, et.seq. California Government Code Section 53646 requires the
  annual review of the City’s Investment Policy at a regular meeting of the City
  Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-30
  adopting the 2020-2021 Statement of Investment Policy.

  E. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 72990 (608 SOUTH RAMONA
  STREET) PLANNING CASE NO. TMAP18-002

  The development, located at 608 South Ramona Street, is a six-unit
  condominium development on two lots totaling 23,924 square feet. City Staff
  and the Los Angeles County Department of Public Works have reviewed the
  Final Tract Map and have determined it is in compliance with the State
  Subdivision Map Act, conditions of approval, and the City’s ordinances
  regarding subdivision.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept the Final Tract Map No. 72990
  and authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 16, 2020  3
   F. APPOINTMENTS TO THE CITY’S COMMISSIONS

  The City solicited applications for vacant and expiring seats on Civil Service,
  Community Services, Design Review, Historic Preservation and Cultural
  Resource, and Planning Commissions for two-year terms from June 2020
  through May 2022. This item is to ratify the City Council’s choices for
  appointments.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the appointments
  recommended by the Mayor.

  G. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO.  664
  ESTABLISHING NON-EXCLUSIVE TOWING SERVICE FRANCHISES

  The City of San Gabriel currently operates its police-initiated tow service
  through an informal agreement, rather than the industry standard franchise
  agreement. While the informal agreement the City used in the past has been
  satisfactory, the benefits of a towing service franchise agreement include a
  reduction in City liability and exposure, better control of the service provided
  to the public, and a method of cost recovery for City administrative costs.
  Ordinance No. 664 was introduced on June 2, 2020, by a 5-0 vote. Adoption
  of this Ordinance would approve the City of San Gabriel to establish non-
  exclusive towing services franchises and authorize entrance into towing
  agreements with qualified tow service providers.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Ordinance No. 664 to establish non-exclusive towing services
  franchises; and
  2. Authorize the City to enter into tow service agreements with qualified tow
  service operators.

5.  PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 16, 2020  4
 6.  NEW BUSINESS

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS APPROVING THE OPERATING BUDGET
  AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AND ESTABLISHING THE
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21

  The City Council will consider the operating budget as it provides a summary
  of the Proposed Budget and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for Fiscal Year
  2020-21. The operating budget, including proposed amendments, totals
  $68,047,732. The CIP totals $6,191,594, providing new/additional funding for
  16 projects.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt:
  1. Resolution No. 20-29 Adopting the City’s Operating Budget for Fiscal Year
  2020-21; and
  2. Resolution No. 20-24 Approving the 2020-21 to 2024-25 Five-Year Capital
  Improvement Program and Adopting a Capital Improvement Program
  Budget for Fiscal Year 2020-21; and
  3. Resolution No. 20-27 Establishing the Gann Appropriations Limit for Fiscal
  Year 2020-21.

  B. ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES AGREEMENT

  In 2012, the City of San Gabriel entered into an agreement with the San
  Gabriel Valley Humane Society (SGVHS) for animal care and control services.
  Since then, the agreement has automatically renewed and has had several
  subsequent rate increases. Most recently, the City was informed by SGVHS
  that a 33% rate increase is to be expected starting Fiscal Year 2020-2021 due
  to several key factors. Staff has worked with the City Attorney’s Office to
  prepare an Animal Care and Control Services Agreement (Agreement) for a
  one-year term, for City Council’s consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve:
  1. The Animal Care and Control Services Agreement with San Gabriel Valley
  Humane Society; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute all necessary documents related to
  this Agreement.

 City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 16, 2020  5
   C. REQUEST TO APPOINT TWO CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS TO A SUB-
  COMMITTEE TO SERVE AS A LIAISON BETWEEN THE CITY COUNCIL AND
  THE COMMUNITY FOR THE COMMUNITY DISCUSSION DESCRIBED IN
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-31

  On June 9, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-31 responding
  to the homicide of George Floyd and committing to engage in a conversation
  with the community regarding the policies and practices throughout the City
  of San Gabriel organization. In order to begin the process and engage
  community stakeholders.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appoint two members to a sub-
  committee to begin the conversation committed to in Resolution No. 20-31

  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, July 7, 2020 at
  6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website

MINUTES OF JUNE 16, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:31 p.m. on Tuesday, June 16, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

Mayor Menchaca provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Council Member Pu requested that New Business items 6A and 6B be considered in
  reversed order as item 6B could have an effect on budget item 6A.
  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Pu, to accept
  the agenda order as amended to consider item 6A after agenda item 6B.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT MANAGER DOMENICA
  MEGERDICHIAN
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 8  June 16, 2020
   Presentation was made by Assistant City Manager/Community Development
  Director Arminé Chaparyan.

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  Mayor Menchaca announced that this will be an ongoing presentation on the
  Agenda until the COVID-19 epidemic ends to keep the public informed directly
  from the City’s first responders and staff.

  Presentations were made by Fire Chief Wallace, Police Chief Harris, and City
  Manager Lazzaretto.

  Discussion ensued on a subcommittee of Council Members to assist with outreach
  to the business community regarding COVID-19-related assistance, with Vice
  Mayor Liao and Council Member Ding agreeing to serve on the committee. The
  matter will be agendized for the next regular City Council meeting.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Debbie Kilgore provided questions regarding police staffing levels proportionate to
  the population and possible results of decreasing police officer positions.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  In response to questions from Vice Mayor Liao regarding Item 4C, City Manager
  Lazzaretto explained that funds from Certificates of Deposit (CDs) which mature are
  reinvested by placing them into the Local Agency Investment Fund, and that the
  Finance Director makes those decisions on a daily basis in accordance with the City’s
  Investment Policy.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4G as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4G as presented by a vote of 5-0 as
  follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following items as presented:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 27, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 2, 2020.
  3. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 2, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the May 22, 2020, and May 27, 2020 Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2020

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 8  June 16, 2020
   The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for May 2020.

  D. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2020-2021

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-30 adopting the 2020-2021
  Statement of Investment Policy.

  E. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 72990 (608 SOUTH RAMONA
  STREET) PLANNING CASE NO. TMAP18-002

  The City Council accepted Final Tract Map No. 72990 and authorized filing with the
  Los Angeles County Recorder.

  F. APPOINTMENTS TO THE CITY’S COMMISSIONS

  The City Council approved the following appointments recommended by the
  Mayor for full terms of two years, expiring on 5/30/2022:

    Community Services Commission: Cheryl Anne Cabot and Theresa Huerta;
    Design Review Commission: Raymond Cheng, Marla Nadolney, and Nik Sae-
  Low;
    Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission: Beatrix Mojarro and
  Kyle DeVriendt; and
    Planning Commission: Mark Juarez, Thomas Klawiter, and Jingbo Lou.

  The City Council approved the following appointment recommended by the Mayor
  for an unexpired term expiring on 5/30/2021:

    Community Services Commission: Wei (Nancy) Fang.

  G. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 664 ESTABLISHING
  NON-EXCLUSIVE TOWING SERVICE FRANCHISES

  The City Council:

  1. Adopted Ordinance No. 664 to establish non-exclusive towing services
  franchises; and
  2. Authorized the City to enter into tow service agreements with qualified tow
  service operators.

5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  B. ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Presentation was made by Assistant City Manager/Community Development
  Director Arminé Chaparyan. San Gabriel Humane Society (SGHS) Board President
  Cindy Rigny was also present virtually to answer questions.

  No public comment was received.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 8  June 16, 2020
   Discussion included value received versus cost; reasons for cost increases including
  minimum wage hikes and an increase in the number of animals; full service versus
  a la carte services; hybrid service models; the SGHS adding additional cities to share
  overhead expenses; effects of the COVID-19 crisis; convenience of SGHS being
  located in the City; SGHS staff pay is less costly than City employee pay; the City
  receives licensing revenue; possibility of licensing cats; partnering for fund-raising
  and provision of other services; the possibility of City representation on the SGHS
  Board; exploring alternative service models over the next year; going without some
  services or having a shorter agreement with SGHS; and numbers and types of calls
  for service.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  a six-month agreement with San Gabriel Humane Society for $175,000, with an
  option to extend the agreement for six months at $175,000.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-1 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

RECESS AND RECONVENE

Mayor Menchaca recessed the meeting at 9:02 p.m. and reconvened the meeting at 9:12
p.m. with all Council Members present.

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS APPROVING THE OPERATING BUDGET AND
  CAPITAL  IMPROVEMENT  PROGRAM  AND  ESTABLISHING THE
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21

  Presentation was made by Interim Finance Director Ken Louie.

  Mayor Menchaca added that although we will have a placeholder for a Budget
  update for the second City Council meeting of each month, if revenues drop or
  expenses increase, an update will be provided sooner.

  The following provided comments in opposition to defunding/reducing the Police
  Department Budget: Lei Wang, San Gabriel business owner; Christine Tureaud;
  Galvin S. Templar, resident; Lynn Snowden, resident; Linda Parmenter; Carla J. Seifi;
  Jing Wu, resident; Rodney Luck, resident; Fion Chan, resident; D. Barrera, resident;
  Brenda, resident; Sue Fitzsimmons; Tracy Ellis, resident; Mirta Isla, resident; Harold
  Jeffs, resident; Marilyn Jeffs, resident; Melanie Lehocz, resident; James L. Perea,
  resident; Linda D. Perea, resident; Alexis Salamanca, President, San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce and San Gabriel business owner; Gloria Sorenson, resident;
  Larry Sorenson, resident; Sophia Tsoi, resident; Alice Wong, resident; Thomas
  Wong, resident; Robert A. Carreon; Melanie L., resident; Gina; Patty Rodriguez,
  resident; Lisa H., resident; Mark Zacher; Brad Cadle; and Anna.

  The following provided comments in favor of reducing the Police Department
  Budget in favor of various other options: Gabriel Frank-McPheter; Joshua
  Raymundo; Chasity Jennings-Nunez and 47 additional individuals.

  Comments not stating a position on this item were also provided by: Charmaine
  Liccardi, resident; Julie Casciani; and Sean McMorris, resident.

  Discussion included the need to listen to all stakeholders; positive reforms Police
  Chief Harris has already implemented to the betterment of the community;
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 8  June 16, 2020
   examining all City government culture, not just in the Police Department; having a
  placeholder for animal control services as the outcome of that agreement is not
  yet known; ad hominem attacks made during public comment and clarification of
  Council Member comments made at the previous City Council meeting; diversion
  or defunding of the Police Department Budget equates to less officers in the field;
  having a back-up plan if the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society (SGVHS) doesn’t
  approve a six-month agreement; adding a social services program without taking
  money from the Police Department budget; keeping bi-lingual pay for police
  officers; budgeting for lawsuit costs; vehicle maintenance costs; ability to make
  budget adjustments in the future; appreciation for the recent civic engagement by
  young-adult residents; commendation for improvements Police Chief Harris and
  the Police Department have made; and having facts before making changes to the
  budget.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to adopt
  the following:

  1. Resolution No. 20-29 Adopting the City’s Operating Budget for Fiscal Year
  2020-21; and
  2. Resolution No. 20-24 Approving the 2020-21 to 2024-25 Five-Year Capital
  Improvement Program and Adopting a Capital Improvement Program Budget
  for Fiscal Year 2020-21; and
  3. Resolution No. 20-27 Establishing the Gann Appropriations Limit for Fiscal
  Year 2020-21.

  Motion approved New Business Item 6A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE
Concern was voiced regarding the late addition of items to the agenda in regard to
allowing time for proper review.

A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao to continue
consideration of agenda item 6C past 11:00 p.m.

Motion carried by a vote of 4-1 as follows:

AYES:  DING, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
NOES:  HARRINGTON
ABSTAIN:  NONE
ABSENT:  NONE

  C. REQUEST TO APPOINT TWO CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS TO A SUB-COMMITTEE
  TO SERVE AS A LIAISON BETWEEN THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE COMMUNITY
  FOR THE COMMUNITY DISCUSSION DESCRIBED IN RESOLUTION NO. 20-31

  Presentation was made by Mayor Menchaca.

  The following provided comments requesting the appointment of Mayor
  Menchaca and Council Member Pu to the sub-committee and requesting that
  Council Member Harrington not be appointed to the sub-committee: Gabriel
  Frank-McPheter; and George Valdez.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 8  June 16, 2020
   The following provided comments in support of the formation of a sub-committee:
  Monica Bouffard, resident; Catherine Cordero, resident; Devyn Cordero, resident;
  Chris Cordero, resident; Joel Cordero, resident; and Chasity Jennings-Nuñez.

  The following provided comments in support of the formation of a subcommittee
  and requesting that Council Member Harrington not be appointed to the sub-
  committee: Alejandra Benavides, resident; and Sean McMorris, resident.

  Cheryl Cabot provided comments requesting the appointment of Mayor Menchaca
  and Council Member Pu to the subcommittee.

  Long Z. Liu, San Gabriel business member, provided comments requesting that the
  sub-committee’s vision be toward bolstering the Police Department.

  Scott Dutra, resident, provided comments requesting that the sub-committee be
  used to create more community programs and to support the Police Department
  with resources.

  Abraham Odabachian provided comments in support of the Police Department.

  A San Gabriel resident provided comments requesting that the City Council not
  support any of the seven demands of Chasity Jennings-Nunez.

  Comments stating we need to listen to our youth were provided by an anonymous
  commenter.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca to appoint herself and Council Member
  Pu to the sub-committee.

  Discussion included concern about the late timing of the placement of this item on
  the agenda; the desire for all members of the City Council to directly engage with
  the community; preference for the Executive Team, City Manager, and Police and
  Fire Chiefs to lead the sub-committee with Chief Harris as the lead, or alternatively,
  to have two rotating Council Members on the sub-committee with all having equal
  right to participate and none appearing consecutively; all stakeholders need to be
  invited and it should stay San Gabriel focused; and having well-announced
  meetings that are audio-recorded.

  Council Member Harrington requested to amend the motion to include setting up
  a community whistle-blower hotline which would be anonymous and have a phone
  line and email monitored by the City Manager, Assistant City Manager and both
  Chiefs, for reporting perceived racism and perceived unequal treatment, with
  oversight from the City Attorney.

  Discussion continued on the sub-committee as a standing committee subject to
  the Brown Act versus an ad hoc committee and associated provisions for each type
  of meeting; and setting up a standing commission on the same topic.

  Vice Mayor Liao seconded the Mayor’s motion.

  Discussion continued on the receipt of comments on both sides of the issue, and
  the length of time and how often the sub-committee would meet.

  City Attorney Lemieux suggested that an ad hoc committee be established to
  determine the goals, composition, length of time and other details for the

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 6 of 8  June 16, 2020
   formation of a committee for the community conversations, at which point we can
  better understand how the Brown Act would apply.

  Discussion continued on the sub-committee as an ad hoc committee to engage
  stakeholders and gather initial information to define a framework of desired goals,
  outcomes and process for the project, pursuant to Resolution 20-31.

  Mayor Menchaca amended her motion, to appoint herself and Council Member Pu
  to an ad hoc sub-committee to gather the initial information and define a
  framework as prescribed by the resolution we passed, Resolution No. 20-31. Vice
  Mayor Liao seconded the amended motion.

  Discussion continued regarding the formation of a standing commission; the time
  frame for the sub-committee to report back to the full Council; the timeline for the
  sub-committee to complete its task; and clarification on the purpose and
  methodology for the sub-committee.

  Mayor Menchaca withdrew her motion with Vice Mayor Liao’s consent. She made
  a new motion, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to appoint Council Member Pu and
  herself for an ad hoc sub-committee with a timeline of two months, with the
  purpose of gathering information and defining the framework for us to move
  forward with the conversations that we committed to with Resolution No. 20-31.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to continue
considering agenda items after 11:00 p.m.

Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
NOES:  NONE
ABSTAIN:  NONE
ABSENT:  NONE

7. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT – None.

9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Ding thanked all the residents for their comments, thanked staff for
  staying with the Council in this meeting past 12:00 a.m., and commented that for the
  future, with our teamwork, residents will like to live in our City.

  Council Member Harrington requested a progress update from City Manager
  Lazzaretto on changing the ordinance regarding variances. City Manager Lazzaretto
  responded that he would send an update to the Council by email and put it on the
  Council agenda for July 7, 2020. Council Member Harrington thanked everyone for
  staying in for the whole meeting.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 7 of 8  June 16, 2020
